newsitem.title: UK: Howard bids to lead British Conservatives.
newsitem.headline: Howard bids to lead British Conservatives.

text.p: Former Home Secretary (interior minister) Michael Howard said on Tuesday he would stand for the leadership of Britain's Conservative Party, defeated by Labour in the May 1 election.

Following John Major's decision to step down as party chief, Howard joins former finance minister Kenneth Clarke, former social security secretary Peter Lilley and John Redwood in the leadership race, expected to be held in early summer.
Howard said the Conservatives, who on May 1 suffered their worst election defeat since 1832, faced a gruelling battle of attrition against the Labour Party, which had its best ever election result.
"I will lead a united party from the front," Howard told a news conference."
Howard confirmed that he and former Welsh Secretary William Hague had reached an agreement to stand as a joint ticket, but Hague had had second thoughts.

Hague, 36, the bookmakers' favourite, has not yet announced whether he will stand. Another front-runner, former deputy prime minister Michael Heseltine, ruled himself out of the race at the weekend after being admitted to hospital with angina.
